## The workflow

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

### Start with prices

Generate two five-year synthetic histories with different volatility.

### Calibrate

Estimate annualized drift and volatility from the last year of returns.

### Simulate

Use those estimates to draw forward scenarios.

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

The same Python functions drive the report and notebook. The dashboard adds
browser-side controls so you can change the asset and lookback window.

**Use the arrows at the screen edges or the left/right keys to move through
the slides.**

:::

:::

## Two toy histories

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "src")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from market_demo import generate_prices

steady = generate_prices(drift=0.07, volatility=0.18, seed=42)
volatile = generate_prices(drift=0.04, volatility=0.34, seed=2026)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.8))
ax.plot(steady.index, steady, color="#087f8c", linewidth=1.8, label="Steady")
ax.plot(volatile.index, volatile, color="#e76f51", linewidth=1.5, label="Volatile")
ax.set(title="Two seeded GBM price histories", xlabel="Date", ylabel="Synthetic price")
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncol=2)
ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Estimate from a window

```{python}
from market_demo import estimate_parameters, log_returns

steady_returns = log_returns(steady)
volatile_returns = log_returns(volatile)
lookback = 252
steady_fit = estimate_parameters(steady_returns.tail(lookback))
volatile_fit = estimate_parameters(volatile_returns.tail(lookback))

print(f"Steady series:   {steady_fit['volatility']:.1%} annualized volatility")
print(f"Volatile series: {volatile_fit['volatility']:.1%} annualized volatility")
```

The dashboard lets you change that lookback from 60 to 1,260 trading days.
Short windows respond faster to recent moves; long windows smooth them out.

## Simulate forward

```{python}
from market_demo import simulate_gbm

forecast_days = 252
paths = simulate_gbm(
    initial_price=float(steady.iloc[-1]),
    n_days=forecast_days,
    drift=steady_fit["drift"],
    volatility=steady_fit["volatility"],
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.8))
ax.plot(paths.index, paths.median(axis=1), color="#087f8c", linewidth=2, label="Median")
ax.fill_between(
    paths.index,
    paths.quantile(0.05, axis=1),
    paths.quantile(0.95, axis=1),
    color="#f4a261",
    alpha=0.28,
    label="5th–95th percentile",
)
ax.set(title="One-year GBM scenarios, calibrated on the steady series",
       xlabel="Trading days from today", ylabel="Synthetic price")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## What to remember

- Log-return standard deviation scales with \(\sqrt{252}\) to annualize volatility.
- The calibration window and chosen series change the estimated parameters.
- GBM is a useful teaching model, not a realistic guarantee about future returns.

**Try the live controls:** open the dashboard and vary the asset and window.
